name: Level-of-Detail Selection

# Level-of-Detail Selection
## Overview
Level-of-Detail Selection is an algorithm that uses an image-based quality metric to select appropriate levels of detail for rendering large volumetric data, thereby improving image quality during real-time rendering [S1]. It builds on [Error-based and Statistical Prediction](15224-error-based-and-statistical-prediction.md) by relying on direct image fidelity metrics rather than precomputed statistical histogram spectra to drive the selection decision [S1].
## How it works
The method operates within a [GPU-based raycasting](#6192-gpu-raycasting.md) pipeline to handle large volumetric datasets [S1].

**Steps:**
1. **Metric Calculation:** An image-based quality metric is computed to evaluate the visual difference between the current LOD and a reference (higher fidelity) LOD [S1].
2. **Selection:** The LOD is selected based on the quality metric to ensure the rendered image meets a quality threshold while optimizing for performance [S1].

## Subtopics

### Residual-Proxy Adaptive Selector
An adaptive [LOD selection](#22744-lod-selection.md) method that uses residual proxies to recover quality over fixed threshold methods at comparable primitive counts [S2, unofficial]. On the 'garden' scene, it recovers 0.49 dB over the fixed threshold at a comparable primitive count (1.05×) [S2, unofficial]. On city-scale models, it renders 68% of the primitives at −0.05 dB loss with [compression](#4-compression.md) factor $c=4$ [S2, unofficial]. The city-scale model exhibits a wider near-lossless window than the garden model because the aerial model is already tessellated at its training viewing distance, exhausting sub-pixel redundancy at small $c$ and leaving surplus in super-pixel collapse [S2, unofficial].

## Background
The method was developed by Wang et al. to provide interactive volume renditions for large volumetric data on the GPU [S1]. It is used in real-time [volume rendering pipelines](#1318-volume-rendering-pipeline.md) where image quality must be maintained while managing computational load [S1]. Block transformation coding for volume compression, which operates in a similar GPU-based pipeline, was previously proposed by Fout and Ma [S1].
